paths.description: Homepage and personalized news feed, representing global chrome, score ticker, navigation, consent, and the primary news-discovery journey.
Football section listing, representing a sport index/listing template and section navigation.
Lead football article, representing the editorial article template, reading journey, structured metadata, and no-JavaScript rendering.
MLB game recap, representing the dense live-score/statistics detail template.
Deliberately unknown route, representing HTTP/navigation failure recovery.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode probe matched prefers-color-scheme: dark but body colors stayed rgb(237, 238, 240) on rgb(72, 73, 74), and the dark screenshot remained the light design.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, control, and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: Motion is not reduced when requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, two 200ms document animations still ran with unchanged duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or substantially shorten non-essential transitions inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The DOM/probe found no view-transition declarations on navigation-heavy homepage and section templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-document and cross-document navigation with View Transitions while retaining instant fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome is fixed/sticky but not state-aware, and overlays use manual positioning.
findings.evidence: Navigation probe found sticky/fixed chrome and aria-haspopup dropdowns, while the feature probe found no container scroll-state or CSS anchor-positioning declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries for sticky chrome and CSS anchor positioning with fallback positions for menus/tooltips.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent wall obscures every representative page on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the privacy dialog blocking all news, article, section, and game content; at 360px the actions are below the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface where legally possible; keep reject/manage actions immediately reachable and preserve content access.

findings.summary: Dialogs and menus are built from role-based/custom elements rather than native top-layer primitives.
findings.evidence: The feature probe counted three role=dialog elements but zero dialog, popover, or details elements; section dropdowns are custom aria-haspopup controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal consent and popover/details for transient menus and disclosure, retaining explicit accessible names and light dismiss.

findings.summary: Dense chrome, side rails, score strips, promotions, and ads compete with editorial content.
findings.evidence: The desktop homepage and section screenshots devote substantial first-viewport space to score chrome, two side rails, account/promotion cards, and consent UI around the lead story.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent side chrome and defer secondary promotions so the lead story and reading flow dominate.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-driven rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The feature probe found no container-type or @container signal despite cards being reused across the center feed and narrower side rails.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards containment and adapt typography/media/layout with container queries, preserving viewport fallback.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target support are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The focus probe showed many score links with outline none, while Lighthouse reported two target-size failures; only some buttons exposed a visible focus outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a consistent :focus-visible indicator and ensure interactive targets meet minimum size and spacing.

findings.summary: Unknown routes fail in an unrecoverable redirect loop.
findings.evidence: The exercised invalid route rendered Chrome ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS instead of a branded 404 with routes back to sports, scores, or home.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a single 404 response with a useful error page, search, home/section links, and no redirect cycle.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance is poor and JavaScript dominates the critical path.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 11.8s, TBT 890ms, and interactive 21.7s (performance 0.37); article LCP was 8.8s and TBT 740ms. HAR recorded 132 requests, 3.20MB transferred, 2.06MB scripts, and parser-blocking head scripts; Lighthouse estimated 1,052KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove/conditionally load unused and third-party JavaScript, defer non-critical head scripts, shorten render-blocking chains, and prioritize the LCP asset.

findings.summary: Many images lack accessible alternatives.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reported 99 of 100 homepage images without alt; Lighthouse confirmed 38 image-alt failures on home and three on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt text to editorial images and explicit empty alt for genuinely decorative images; expose equivalent score/team names where icons are decorative.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI have repeated contrast failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 29 contrast failures on the homepage and one on the article; forced-colors remained usable, so the failure is in authored colors rather than platform high-contrast support.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise foreground/background contrast to WCAG minimums while keeping forced-colors behavior intact.

findings.summary: The viewport disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: The live viewport meta is initial-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no, and Lighthouse failed the meta-viewport accessibility audit on home and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1.0; verify 200–400% zoom/reflow without loss of content or controls.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime errors and uses deprecated APIs and malformed image presentation.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported two console-error entries, one deprecation warning, and three incorrect-aspect-ratio images on the homepage; best-practices scored 0.73.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the recorded console/network errors, replace the deprecated API, and preserve image intrinsic aspect ratios.

findings.summary: Several visible controls use non-crawlable placeholder links and one link has weak text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found four non-crawlable anchors and one non-descriptive link; recon showed prominent controls such as Buscar, Deportes, Disney+, and score filters resolving to #.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for local state controls and real descriptive href values for navigation destinations.

findings.summary: Cookies and transport defenses are not secure by default.
findings.evidence: Cookie audit found all 17 cookies flagged insecure, including 16 without Secure and many SameSite=None; HSTS and nosniff were absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure and suitable SameSite on HTTPS cookies, remove unnecessary identifiers, and add HSTS plus X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.summary: The initial page load has a disproportionate third-party and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR classified 127 of 132 requests and 3.15MB of 3.20MB as cross-origin; tracker audit found 26 third-party origins plus DoubleClick/Google ad trackers before consent was resolved. The two API keys are public Braze SDK identifiers and the private-key match is library source, not exposed credentials.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential advertising/analytics until consent, reduce vendors, batch telemetry, and load account/personalization SDKs only when invoked.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The response had only a frame-ancestors CSP directive; Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy were absent, as were HSTS and nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive full CSP, explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, HSTS, and nosniff; retain frame-ancestors for clickjacking protection.

findings.summary: Image delivery omits intrinsic dimensions and responsive loading on many images.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 100/100 images without width/height, 23 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 17 without srcset, and four oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, and lazy loading for below-fold images while prioritizing the LCP image.

taskList.title: Cut critical JavaScript, third-party work, and render-blocking chains
Restore accessible image alternatives, zoom, focus, target sizes, and contrast
Replace the unknown-route redirect loop with a useful 404
Secure cookies and deploy complete browser security policies
Make consent content-first and use native dialog/popover primitives
Add preference-driven dark and reduced-motion styles
Optimize responsive image delivery and intrinsic sizing
Fix crawlable navigation links and document/platform errors
Reduce non-content chrome and modernize responsive/navigation components
